issues.explanation: The skill clearly enables network-capable scraping, browser automation, and crawling, but it does not declare an explicit tool scope such as permissions or allowed-tools. In an agent environment, missing scope boundaries can cause over-broad invocation and allow the skill to perform network actions without clear policy constraints or user awareness.
issues.remediation: Add explicit tool/permission declarations for network access and any file-write capabilities. Document the minimum required scope, restrict invocation to approved tools only, and ensure the agent runtime enforces user confirmation for outbound network use.

issues.explanation: The description says to use the skill whenever asked to scrape, crawl, extract data, when web_fetch fails, for anti-bot protected sites, or to write Python scraping code. That broad routing can cause the agent to invoke a powerful network/browser automation skill for common coding requests, increasing the chance of unnecessary external access or misuse.
issues.remediation: Narrow the invocation criteria to clearly bounded scraping tasks, require explicit user intent for live network access, and separate documentation/code-generation use cases from execution-capable scraping workflows.

issues.explanation: The Docker reference `docker pull pyd4vinci/scrapling` omits a fixed tag or digest, so users may pull a different image over time than the one reviewed. This weakens supply-chain integrity and reproducibility, and could expose users to a malicious or compromised image if the upstream tag changes.
issues.remediation: Pin the Docker image to a specific immutable version tag and preferably a digest, such as `image:version@sha256:...`. Update documentation to recommend only reviewed, pinned images and establish a process for verifying image provenance.

issues.explanation: Using the `latest` tag for `ghcr.io/d4vinci/scrapling:latest` makes the deployed artifact mutable and unpredictable. If the upstream image is replaced or compromised, users may execute unreviewed code with network and browser automation capabilities.
issues.remediation: Replace `:latest` with a specific reviewed version and ideally a digest. Include guidance for signature/provenance verification and a documented update process for moving to newer vetted versions.

issues.explanation: The skill instructs saving fetched content to files and even recommends temp-file workflows, but it does not warn about path safety, overwrites, or sensitive local file destinations. In an agent setting, this can lead to unintended overwriting of user files or writing untrusted remote content to unsafe locations.
issues.remediation: Add explicit warnings and safeguards for file writes: require user-approved output paths, default to securely created temporary files, prevent overwriting unless explicitly confirmed, and sanitize or constrain writable destinations.

issues.explanation: The documentation recommends enabling `development_mode = True`, which caches fetched responses to disk for later replay. In a scraping skill that handles arbitrary remote content, this can persist sensitive pages, session-derived content, or regulated data locally if users forget to disable it or do not control the cache location properly.
issues.remediation: Add a stronger warning that development caching stores remote content on disk and may retain sensitive data. Default the example to an isolated temporary cache path, document cache cleanup procedures, and recommend disabling the feature unless the data being cached is explicitly non-sensitive and user-approved.
